title: Reviewing a design with peers
idea: A design peer review is a short session where others test your classes against the requirements, and you record each finding with the change it asks for.
points: Present the requirements first, then walk one use case through your classes.
Reviewers ask questions about the design, not about your naming taste.
Each comment names a problem, a concrete scenario and a suggested change.
You leave with a short list of fixes, ranked by how much they matter.

hero.title: A review checklist
head: Area
Question to ask
Red flag
rows: Does every must-have action have a method?
A use case with no owner
Can each class be described in one sentence?
One class does most of the work
What changes if a new type or rule arrives?
Editing a switch in several places
What if two users act at the same moment?
Check, then act, with no guard
Can the core flow run with a fake clock and no network?
Hidden new Date() or global state
hero.caption: Ask these in order. Each red flag points at a concrete fix, not a matter of taste.

quiz.q: Which review comment is the most useful?
options: I would have used different class names.
Two users can book one room; lock inside `book()`.
Consider using more design patterns here.
quiz.why: It names a scenario, the code that fails and a fix. The others are opinions with nothing to act on.

takeaway: Good review comments name a scenario, a failure and a fix.

starters: How do I respond when a reviewer disagrees with my design choice?
